title: Journalist & Whistleblower Privacy for Beginners
metaDescription: Learn essential privacy tools and practices for journalists and whistleblowers. Secure communication, source protection, and digital safety guide.
intro: Journalists and whistleblowers face unique digital security challenges when protecting sources and sensitive information. This guide covers essential privacy tools and practices to maintain confidentiality, secure communications, and protect both yourself and your sources from surveillance and retaliation.
prerequisites: Understanding of email and messaging apps
Willingness to change current communication habits

steps.title: Secure Your Basic Digital Footprint
steps.description: Start by securing your fundamental online presence and communications to create a foundation for source protection.
actions: Use a privacy-focused browser like Incognito Browser for all research
Create separate email accounts for sensitive communications using ProtonMail or Tutanota
Enable two-factor authentication on all important accounts
Use strong, unique passwords with a password manager like Bitwarden
Review and tighten privacy settings on social media accounts
steps.proTip: Create a completely separate digital identity for sensitive journalism work, including new email accounts and social media profiles.

steps.title: Set Up Encrypted Communication Channels
steps.description: Establish secure communication methods that protect both you and your sources from surveillance and interception.
actions: Install Signal messenger for encrypted text and voice communications
Set up disappearing messages in Signal (24 hours or less)
Learn to use SecureDrop if your organization has it available
Create a Tor browser setup for anonymous web browsing
Set up a VPN service like ExpressVPN or NordVPN for additional protection
steps.proTip: Always verify Signal safety numbers when communicating with sources to ensure your connection hasn't been compromised.
steps.warning: Never use regular SMS, email, or phone calls for sensitive source communications - these can be easily intercepted.

steps.title: Implement Source Protection Protocols
steps.description: Develop and follow strict protocols to protect your sources' identities and maintain their anonymity throughout your reporting process.
actions: Use encrypted note-taking apps like Standard Notes for interview notes
Store sensitive files on encrypted external drives, not cloud services
Meet sources in public places away from cameras and recording devices
Use cash for expenses related to source meetings to avoid digital trails
Establish code words or phrases for emergency communications with sources
steps.proTip: Create a source protection checklist and follow it religiously for every sensitive story you work on.
steps.warning: Never store source names or identifying information in the same location as the information they provide.

steps.title: Practice Operational Security (OPSEC)
steps.description: Develop habits and procedures that minimize your digital footprint and protect against surveillance by both criminals and state actors.
actions: Use burner phones for sensitive communications, replaced regularly
Leave personal devices at home when meeting sources
Cover laptop cameras and use headphones to prevent audio surveillance
Vary your routes and meeting locations to avoid pattern recognition
Regularly audit your digital accounts for unusual activity
steps.proTip: Think like someone is always watching your digital activities, because they might be. Assume all communications are potentially monitored.
steps.warning: Border crossings pose special risks - consider using clean devices and storing sensitive data separately when traveling.

steps.title: Secure Information Storage and Handling
steps.description: Establish secure methods for storing, organizing, and accessing sensitive information while maintaining source confidentiality.
actions: Use full-disk encryption on all devices (FileVault for Mac, BitLocker for Windows)
Store sensitive documents in encrypted containers using VeraCrypt
Implement a secure backup strategy using encrypted external drives
Use metadata removal tools before sharing documents or images
Establish secure document destruction procedures for physical materials
steps.proTip: Create multiple encrypted containers - one for each sensitive story - to compartmentalize information and reduce risk.
steps.warning: Cloud storage services can be subpoenaed. Even encrypted cloud services may not protect you from legal compulsion to provide passwords.

faqs.question: What should I do if I think I'm under surveillance?
faqs.answer: Stop all sensitive activities immediately, vary your daily routines, use only previously established secure communication channels, and consider consulting with digital security experts or press freedom organizations like the Committee to Protect Journalists.

faqs.question: Is it legal to use these privacy tools?
faqs.answer: Yes, using encryption and privacy tools is legal in most countries. However, laws vary by jurisdiction, and some countries restrict or monitor these tools. Research your local laws and consider the legal environment where you're working.

faqs.question: How do I balance transparency with source protection?
faqs.answer: Be transparent about your methods and verification processes without revealing identifying details. Use phrases like 'a government source' or 'documents obtained by this reporter' while protecting specific identities and methods.

faqs.question: What if my organization doesn't support these security measures?
faqs.answer: Start with personal security measures you can implement independently. Educate colleagues and management about the importance of source protection. Consider reaching out to press freedom organizations for support and resources.

faqs.question: How often should I update my security practices?
faqs.answer: Review and update your security practices every 3-6 months, or immediately after any security incident. Stay informed about new threats and tools through organizations like Freedom of the Press Foundation and Committee to Protect Journalists.
